title: radio divider or
rule: Use a radio divider (usually “or”) for an unlike option.
pass_when: An unlike option (e.g. “None of these”, “I don’t know”) is separated with a divider, usually “or”.
fail_when: Unlike option sits in the same undifferentiated list as the similar options.
overview: Separate an unlike radio option with a divider, usually the word or.
apply_when: A radio list includes an unlike option such as none or I don’t know.
not_when: Not for homogeneous option lists with no unlike escape choice.
agent_hint: Insert an or divider before unlike options like None of these.
description: Unlike options—for example “None of these” or “I don’t know”—should be separated from similar options with a radio divider, usually “or”. The divider signals that the escape choice is different from the main set. Leaving it undifferentiated makes the unlike option look like just another similar answer. Fail when the unlike option sits in the same undifferentiated list as the similar choices. Apply when a radio list includes an unlike escape option.
do_not_claim: That every set needs a divider.
